newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE coffee reverses to end down.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE coffee reverses to end down.

text.p: Robusta coffee futures reversed from earlier uptrend to finish lower on trade and speculative profit-taking but renewed roaster buying at the lows helped slow the fall.
Fresh falls in New York also provided further selling impetus.
There were no new market-moving news but traders noted news rains helping Brazilian crop and that Mexico and Colombia were seeking to significantly raise production in the coming years.
Activity in London was centred on two nearby months March and May as some players rolled the March position forward.
March finished $20 down at $1,520 a tonne while May gave up $24 at $1,536 after a high of $1,575.
Active March/May switch was mostly traded at between $15-$20.
Volume totalled 6,861 lots.
The March open positions dropped by a sharp 2,158 lots at Thursday's close to 9,142 ahead of the contract's first delivery day on March 3.
The market was earlier supported by trade buying. Price-fixing by roasters gathered momentum in the afternoon as prices made their way lower.
London's calmer mood was a departure from the past few sessions which saw prices taking sharp swings on volatile New York.
The March/March differential between London and New York stayed at a wide 105 cents a lb.
Looking ahead, traders said the market, shadowing New York, is expected remain volatile with prices fluctuating widely between $1,450 and $1,700 a tonne basis May.
But robusta's downside potential will be underpinned by industry buying on the back of its hefty differential to arabicas.
"I think London will hold relatively well further into the year," he said. "Obviously that doesn't take into account the weather revenge."
Traders said the real key is the size of Brazil's 1997/98 crop which will provide the market direction.
So far, figures from the Brazilian industry suggest that the crop will be 23 million 60-kg bags or below.
Traders said even at 25 million bags there would not be sufficient coffee to meet demand.
With roasters maintaining their hand-to-mouth buying policy, any disruption to supplies will make the market nervous.

News from Brazil said rains over the past two months in Brazil's coffee areas had been beneficial for bean formation but cooperative officials saw no reason to revise up 1997/98 crop forecasts of a maximum 20 million bags.

But Brazil's Unicafe in its first estimat on Friday put the crop at between 19.7 and 22.5 million bags. This compares with another Brazilian industry group Abecafe who this week pegged the crop at 23.2 million which was nearer to earlier trade expectations of 24-25 million. -- Jalil Hamid, London newsroom +44 171 542 4985
